newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHARE VOLUMES GAIN, RTF JUMPS ON Q1.
newsitem.headline: SHARE VOLUMES GAIN, RTF JUMPS ON Q1.

text.p: Shares showed slight signs of recovery on Monday after last week's lows and some blue-chips gained ground, dealers said.
Total turnover rose to 171,000 lats against 76,000 lats and the Rietumu Bank index rose 1.66 pct to 178.97.
Stocks were generally quiet while some blue-chips, including Riga Transport Fleet and Unibanka gained ground.
RTF jumped to 1.40 lats from 1.29 lats. It had a comparatively small volume of 5,600 lats. Dealers said the shares rose after last week's Q1 figures.
"Following a cautious attitude to RTF after it showed a small 1996 profit, the first quarter figures revived some interest," said Girts Ozols, Hansabank-Latvija dealer.
"It still depends how widespread that will be, but RTF at least will not fall further," he added.
RTF last week said its first quarter profit together with subsidiaries came to 1.17 million lats. It had earlier posted 1996 profit of 182,719 lats.
Last week saw a spate of shareholders meetings and dealers said shares blocked for the meetings was one of the key reasons that bourse volumes fell to near record lows.
"There is a certain revival, another question is how quickly this upward trend will grow," Ozols said.
Unibanka continued its recent fluctuations and rose to 3.50 from 3.45 lats on volume of 10,500 lats while fellow official list Staburadze confectionery saw a small volume of 800 lats.
Daugavpils Chain saw the bourse's biggest trade of 28,500 lats and remained stable at 2.35 lats.
Kaija fish cannery added three santimes to 2.26 lats on trade of 6,800 lats. A final decision on when Kaija will be included on the official list is expected this week.
Activity in general was rather low as some 17 secondary list stocks were not quoted.
